body.text: 1. What is Microsoft Excel?
Microsoft Excel is a spreadsheet application developed by Microsoft. It is used to organize, calculate, analyze and visualize data efficiently.
Excel is widely used in schools, colleges, businesses, hospitals, banks and government organizations for maintaining records, preparing reports and performing calculations.
Microsoft Excel is one of the world's most widely used spreadsheet applications.
2. Workbook
A Workbook is an Excel file. It contains one or more worksheets. The default Excel file extension is .xlsx.
3. Worksheet
A Worksheet is a single spreadsheet page inside a workbook where users enter and organize data.
4. Rows and Columns
Rows run horizontally and are identified using numbers. Columns run vertically and are identified using letters.
5. Cell and Cell Address
A Cell is the intersection of a row and a column. Every cell has a unique address.
6. Ribbon
The Ribbon is the command area located at the top of Excel. It contains all tools required for working with worksheets.
7. Formula Bar
The Formula Bar displays the content or formula of the selected cell.
8. Name Box
The Name Box displays the address of the currently selected cell. You can also jump directly to any cell by typing its address.
9. Common Keyboard Shortcuts
Mastering these basics makes learning formulas, functions, charts, Pivot Tables and dashboards much easier.

questions.question: What is Microsoft Excel primarily used for?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Excel is a spreadsheet application used for storing, organizing, analyzing, and calculating data.

questions.question: What is an Excel Workbook?
questions.explanation: A Workbook is an Excel file that contains one or more worksheets.

questions.question: Which of the following represents a valid cell address?
questions.explanation: A valid cell address is formed using the column letter followed by the row number.

questions.question: Rows in Excel are identified using:
questions.explanation: Rows are numbered 1, 2, 3, and so on.

questions.question: Columns in Excel are identified using:
questions.explanation: Columns are labeled A, B, C, D, and so on.

questions.question: What is the intersection of a row and a column called?
questions.explanation: The intersection of a row and column is called a Cell.

questions.question: Which Excel component displays formulas and cell contents?
questions.explanation: The Formula Bar displays the contents or formula of the active cell.

questions.question: Which component contains commands like Home, Insert, Formulas, and Data?
questions.explanation: The Ribbon organizes all Excel commands into different tabs.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut saves the current workbook?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + S saves the current workbook.

questions.question: The Name Box in Excel displays:
questions.explanation: The Name Box displays the address of the currently selected cell, such as A1 or C5.

chapters.title: Day 2: Data Entry, Editing, AutoFill and Flash Fill

concept.title: Entering, Editing and Managing Data in Microsoft Excel

body.text: 1. What is Data Entry?

Data Entry is the process of entering information into Microsoft Excel worksheets. Every piece of information entered into Excel is stored inside a cell. Excel supports different types of data such as text, numbers, dates, time, currency, percentages, and formulas.
Every value entered in Excel is stored in a cell identified by its unique cell address such as A1, B5, or C10.
2. Methods of Entering Data
There are several ways to enter data into Excel. The easiest method is to click a cell, type the required information, and press Enter.

rows: Type directly into the selected cell.
Type or edit data using the Formula Bar.
Paste data copied from another worksheet or application.
Import data from CSV, Text, or external databases.

body.text: 3. Editing Data
Editing means modifying existing data without deleting the entire worksheet. Excel provides several methods for editing cell contents.

items: Press F2 to edit the active cell.
Replace the existing value by typing a new value.

body.text: Editing data does not change the worksheet structure. It only changes the contents of the selected cell.
4. AutoFill
AutoFill is a powerful Excel feature that automatically fills cells with a series of values or copies existing values and formulas. It saves time by reducing repetitive typing.
Drag the small square (Fill Handle) located at the bottom-right corner of the selected cell to use AutoFill.
5. Flash Fill
Flash Fill automatically detects patterns in your data and fills the remaining cells without requiring formulas. It is commonly used to split names, combine text, or extract specific information.
Flash Fill recognizes patterns based on the examples you provide. It does not use formulas.
6. Difference Between AutoFill and Flash Fill

rows: Copies values, formulas or creates series

body.text: 7. Best Practices

items: Always verify data after using Flash Fill.
Use AutoFill for repetitive numeric or date sequences.
Use Flash Fill for text formatting and extraction.
Use Undo (Ctrl + Z) if mistakes occur.
Data Entry is the process of entering information into Excel cells.
Editing allows existing data to be modified.
AutoFill copies values, formulas and creates series automatically.
Flash Fill recognizes patterns and fills data without formulas.
AutoFill and Flash Fill improve productivity and reduce manual work.

questions.question: What is Data Entry in Excel?
questions.explanation: Data Entry is the process of entering information such as text, numbers, dates, and formulas into Excel cells.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid types of data in Excel?
questions.explanation: Excel supports various data types including text, numbers, dates, time, currency, percentages, and formulas.

questions.question: Which key is used to edit the active cell?
questions.explanation: Pressing F2 allows you to edit the contents of the active cell.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of AutoFill?
options: Copy data, formulas, or create a series automatically
questions.explanation: AutoFill automatically copies values, formulas, and generates sequences such as numbers, dates, and months.

questions.question: Where is the Fill Handle located?
options: Bottom-right corner of the selected cell
questions.explanation: The Fill Handle is the small square located at the bottom-right corner of the selected cell.

questions.question: What is Flash Fill mainly used for?
options: Recognizing patterns and automatically filling data
questions.explanation: Flash Fill automatically recognizes patterns in data and fills the remaining cells without formulas.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut activates Flash Fill?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + E is the shortcut key for Flash Fill.

questions.question: What is the main difference between AutoFill and Flash Fill?
options: AutoFill creates series or copies formulas, while Flash Fill recognizes patterns in data.
AutoFill edits worksheets, while Flash Fill saves files.
AutoFill creates charts, while Flash Fill creates tables.
questions.explanation: AutoFill copies values, formulas, and sequences, whereas Flash Fill automatically recognizes patterns in text data.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut performs Undo?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + Z is used to undo the last action performed in Excel.

questions.question: How do you move to the next column while entering data?
questions.explanation: Pressing the Tab key moves the active cell to the next column.
